The privacy threat arises from the source action of granting or initiating access without adequate checks on legitimacy, authority, or appropriateness.
assumptions: Assumes the system permits a parent to initiate invitations before backend verification of authority or policy constraints.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for unawareness/non-compliance around insufficient authorization or expectation management.

title: Invitation data in transit may identify the child, parent, or invited guardian
description: Data sent from the parent to the backend may include names, email addresses, phone numbers, account identifiers, or relationship labels that directly identify the involved parties. If exposed in transit or through observable metadata, the flow can reveal who is connected to whom.
assumptions: Assumes the invitation payload or associated metadata contains direct identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Exact identification subtree node may vary; chosen as best-fit direct identification in transit.

title: Invitation metadata can link parent, child, and secondary guardian
description: Even if payload contents are protected, traffic metadata and backend-facing request structure can reveal that a specific parent account is associating a specific secondary guardian with a specific child account. This creates a new link between individuals and roles within a family network.
assumptions: Assumes the backend or an observer can correlate account identifiers, invitation tokens, or relationship metadata across requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via metadata/correlation on the flow.

title: Relationship and caregiving context may be disclosed through invitation metadata
description: The invitation flow may disclose sensitive contextual information such as that the child is under active location monitoring, that the parent relies on another caregiver, or the nature of the family relationship (e.g. grandparent, relative). Such contextual disclosure can occur through payload fields, logs, headers, or observable communication patterns.
assumptions: Assumes invitation requests include relationship labels or child-sharing context.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended as contextual information disclosure in transit.

title: Backend may store excessive invitation details
description: On receipt, the backend may retain more personal data than necessary about the invitation, such as the invited guardian's contact details, relationship label, child identifiers, timestamps, and access rationale. Excessive storage increases the privacy impact of later misuse or breach.
assumptions: Assumes invitation events and payloads are logged or persisted beyond what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure caused by destination-side storage/processing; exact node may differ.

title: Backend can correlate family-network relationships across accounts
description: By processing the invitation, the backend can link the parent, child, and secondary guardian into a family graph. This may enable broader profiling of household structure, caregiving patterns, and social relationships beyond what is needed to fulfill the invitation.
assumptions: Assumes backend stores account associations and can query them across families or over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side linkability through correlation.

title: Backend processing may identify the invited guardian or child from invitation data
description: The backend may resolve contact details or account references to specific individuals, thereby identifying the invited guardian and associating them with a particular child and parent. This identification may exceed what users expect if done before acceptance or without transparency.
assumptions: Assumes backend can match invitation contact details to existing accounts or external identity records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side identification through received data.

title: Users may be unaware of how invitation data is processed and who can gain access
description: The backend may process the invitation in ways not obvious to the parent, child, or co-guardian, such as pre-creating associations, notifying existing accounts, or exposing pending invitations in account interfaces. Lack of clear notice and understandable controls can leave data subjects unaware of the consequences of the invitation.
assumptions: Assumes the service does not clearly explain invitation handling, visibility, and access effects.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for destination-side unawareness due to opaque processing.

title: Backend may process invitation data without sufficient legal basis or policy compliance
description: The backend's receipt and processing of invitation data may violate applicable child-privacy, consent, guardianship, or data-minimization obligations if it enables sharing before verifying authority, consent, or necessity. This creates a non-compliance risk tied to destination-side processing.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdiction or policy requires verification of parental authority, consent, or minimization before enabling sharing of a child's location.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Backend discloses child's live location to a secondary guardian without valid authorization or consent
description: The backend's act of granting access and sharing the child's live location may disclose highly sensitive real-time location data to EE3 without a valid legal basis, parental authorization, or the child's/primary guardian's informed consent. This is a direct disclosure caused by the source element deciding to share the data.
assumptions: Assumes access control, consent, or guardianship status may be incomplete, outdated, or insufficiently verified before sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized disclosure by the source; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Secondary guardian receives location access without sufficient transparency or user awareness
description: If the backend grants EE3 access without clearly informing the child or primary guardian about what live location data is shared, with whom, and under what conditions, data subjects may be unaware of the processing and disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes notices, in-app indicators, or consent dialogs may be absent, unclear, or not timely.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for lack of awareness/transparency at the source.

title: Live location data in transit can identify the child
description: The data flow contains precise live location information associated with a specific child and guardian relationship. Interception or observation of this flow could directly identify the child or make them identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries account, relationship, or session context in addition to location coordinates or map data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from data in transit; exact subtree may differ.

title: Repeated live-location updates enable linkability of the child's movements over time
description: Because the flow shares live location continuously or repeatedly, observations of the transmitted updates can be linked together to build a movement history for the same child, even if individual messages are pseudonymous.
assumptions: Assumes recurring updates, stable identifiers, tokens, or consistent communication patterns are present.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability across multiple observations of the same flow.

title: Communication metadata reveals that a specific guardian is monitoring a specific child
description: Even aside from payload contents, metadata such as endpoints, timing, frequency, and relationship context in the flow may disclose that EE3 has been granted monitoring access to the child's live location.
assumptions: Assumes network, application, or service metadata is observable to intermediaries or logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure via metadata on the data flow.

title: Secondary guardian may further disclose or misuse the child's live location
description: Once EE3 receives the child's live location, they may store, screenshot, share, or otherwise disclose it to unauthorized parties, causing additional privacy harm at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes EE3's device, account, or behavior is not fully controlled by the system owner.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure arising from recipient-side handling.

title: Secondary guardian can link live location with other knowledge about the child
description: EE3 may combine received live location with prior knowledge, messages, schedules, or other datasets to link the child's identity, habits, school, home, and routines across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes EE3 has auxiliary information about the child or household.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for recipient-side linkability through data combination.

title: Secondary guardian can infer sensitive attributes from the child's live location
description: By observing the child's real-time and historical whereabouts, EE3 can infer sensitive information such as home address, school, religious attendance, medical visits, social relationships, and daily routines.
assumptions: Assumes location is sufficiently precise and frequent to support inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for inferability at the destination from received location data.

title: Shared analytics may enable cross-context linkage by the partner
description: Even if the backend shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics, the chosen aggregation dimensions, cohort sizes, timestamps, campaign identifiers, app version, region, or device-class breakdowns may allow the advertising/analytics partner to link this dataset with other datasets it already holds, connecting app behavior to existing partner-side profiles or segments.
assumptions: Assumes the partner receives analytics with enough granularity or stable dimensions to correlate with other partner-held data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via shared data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Aggregated analytics may still identify individuals or very small groups
description: If aggregation thresholds are weak, rare-behavior cohorts are included, or dimensions are too specific, the shared analytics can single out a user or a very small group, allowing the partner to infer who generated the activity.
assumptions: Assumes small-cell counts, sparse segments, or quasi-identifiers are present in the shared analytics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from insufficient aggregation/k-anonymity; exact node id may differ.

title: Shared engagement analytics may disclose sensitive interests or behaviors
description: Usage and engagement metrics can reveal sensitive traits or interests when broken down by feature, content category, time pattern, geography, or campaign response. Even in aggregate, such disclosures can expose information about vulnerable cohorts or niche user groups to the partner.
assumptions: Assumes analytics dimensions include feature/content categories or other attributes from which sensitive inferences can be drawn.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of information through shared analytics; exact node id may vary.

title: Partner may combine received analytics with its broader ecosystem data
description: On receipt, the advertising/analytics partner may merge the analytics with data from other apps, websites, ad campaigns, or brokered sources, increasing the ability to link cohorts or inferred users across contexts and services.
assumptions: Assumes the partner operates across multiple clients or has access to external datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side linking/combination; exact node id may differ.

title: Partner may re-identify users or cohorts from received analytics
description: The partner may use auxiliary information, historical observations, or campaign data to re-identify individuals or narrow aggregated cohorts to specific persons, especially where cohorts are small or temporally precise.
assumptions: Assumes the partner has auxiliary datasets and the shared analytics retain useful granularity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side re-identification using auxiliary data; exact node id may vary.

title: Partner may infer additional private information from analytics
description: The recipient can analyze engagement patterns to infer interests, habits, demographics, or potentially sensitive attributes about the app's user base or subgroups beyond what was explicitly shared.
assumptions: Assumes the partner performs profiling or inference over the received analytics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side disclosure/inference; exact node id may differ.

title: Secondary advertising use may be unexpected by users
description: Users may reasonably expect analytics to support app operations, but not expect their usage and engagement data—even in aggregated form—to be shared with an advertising/analytics partner to fund the free tier. This creates an unawareness risk about recipients and purposes.
assumptions: Assumes the sharing purpose and recipient are not made sufficiently clear in the user-facing privacy notice or in-product messaging.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness about sharing purpose/recipient; exact node id may vary.

title: Sharing for advertising/monetization may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: If users did not validly consent to partner sharing, or if the privacy notice/purpose limitation does not clearly cover monetization-oriented analytics disclosure, the backend's transfer may be non-compliant with applicable privacy obligations.
assumptions: Assumes a legal basis, consent, legitimate-interest balancing, contractual restriction, or purpose limitation may be missing or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance due to inadequate legal basis/purpose limitation; exact node id may vary.

title: Partner retention or onward sharing may violate agreed limits
description: After receipt, the partner may retain the analytics longer than necessary, repurpose them for its own advertising ecosystem, or onward-share derived insights in ways that exceed contractual terms, user expectations, or regulatory constraints.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient contractual, technical, or audit controls over partner use, retention, and onward transfer.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side non-compliance/secondary use; exact node id may vary.

title: Child discloses precise real-time location and distress status by initiating SOS/check-in
description: By sending a manual check-in or SOS, the child actively reveals highly sensitive personal data: current location and the fact that they may be in distress or require attention. This disclosure occurs at the source because the act of sharing itself exposes sensitive context about the child.
assumptions: The message contains precise or near-real-time location and an SOS/check-in indicator tied to the child.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether the taxonomy separates location and special-category/safety-related disclosures.

title: Message contents or metadata in transit can identify the child
description: The transmitted SOS/check-in payload and associated metadata can directly or indirectly identify the child, for example through account identifiers, device identifiers, session tokens, or precise location that singles them out.
assumptions: Identifiers or sufficiently precise location/context travel with the flow.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from data in transit.

title: Repeated check-ins/SOS events can be linked to build the child's movement pattern
description: Even if individual messages are expected, repeated transmissions over time can be linked using stable identifiers, network metadata, or recurring location points, enabling reconstruction of the child's routines and relationships.
assumptions: The backend or intermediaries can correlate multiple events from the same child/device/account over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability across multiple messages/events.

title: Traffic metadata reveals sensitive behavior even without reading content
description: Observation of timing, frequency, sender/recipient association, and the occurrence of an SOS/check-in transmission may disclose that the child is at a particular place, following a routine, or experiencing an emergency, even if payload confidentiality is otherwise protected.
assumptions: An observer can access communication metadata or infer event occurrence from traffic patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact subtree for disclosure via communication metadata may differ.

title: Backend can link SOS/check-ins with existing child and family profiles
description: Upon receipt, the backend can associate the event with the child's account, parent account, device history, prior locations, and other behavioral records, increasing the ability to correlate data across contexts and over time.
assumptions: P1 stores account-level identifiers and historical event/location data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for recipient-side linkability through aggregation.

title: Backend processing makes the child readily identifiable
description: The backend may combine the incoming location/SOS message with account registration data, device identifiers, or family relationship data so that the child is uniquely identifiable within the system and potentially to operators or downstream systems.
assumptions: P1 has access to registration/profile data tied to the child.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side identifiability through data combination.

title: Backend stores or exposes sensitive location and emergency information
description: The backend's receipt and storage of the message can disclose sensitive information about the child's whereabouts, routines, and possible emergency status to internal staff, integrated services, or unauthorized parties if access controls, minimization, or retention are inadequate.
assumptions: P1 stores message content and location, and these may be accessible beyond the immediate delivery purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for destination-side information disclosure from storage/processing.

title: Backend can use the SOS/check-in data for purposes unexpected by the child
description: The child may intend the message solely to notify a parent, but the backend could use the data for analytics, profiling, safety scoring, service improvement, or sharing with third parties in ways not expected by the child.
assumptions: Secondary use beyond immediate message delivery is technically or organizationally possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unexpected secondary use at the recipient.

title: Child may lack awareness or meaningful control over how SOS/location data is processed
description: Because the sender is a child and the event may be urgent, they may not understand what data is collected, how long it is retained, who can access it, or whether it is reused beyond notifying the parent, undermining informed consent and control.
assumptions: The service provides limited just-in-time notice or granular controls appropriate for children.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/consent-transparency concerns involving children's data.
